projects.title: Plant Health Monitoring System
projects.summary: LeafAI is a plant health application that classifies plant diseases from leaf images. It combines a fine-tuned MobileNetV2 model with a Flask REST API to make image-based predictions accessible through a web application.
projects.problem: Identifying plant diseases from leaf images requires interpreting visual symptoms. The project explores how computer vision can make this process faster and more accessible through an image-based prediction workflow.
projects.solution: A MobileNetV2 transfer-learning model was fine-tuned with TensorFlow and Keras, then integrated into a Flask REST API that accepts leaf images and returns disease predictions. CNN architectures were compared to guide model selection before integrating the selected model into the application.
projects.deployment: React frontend and Flask API configured on Render
projects.contribution: On our six-person senior design project, I was the sole Computer Science student, working with five AI teammates to bring the team’s MobileNetV2 plant disease model into a Flask application. I focused on connecting leaf-image input, model inference, and the prediction shown to the user.
projects.keyFeature: Image-based plant disease classification through a REST endpoint, connecting the trained computer vision model to an application workflow.
projects.technicalChallenge: Selecting a CNN architecture for plant disease classification and taking the model from training experiments to inference within a Flask application.
highlights: Fine-tuned a MobileNetV2 transfer-learning model for plant disease classification
Compared CNN architectures to guide model selection and reduce experimentation time
Delivered a REST endpoint for real-time prediction from leaf images

architecture.title: LeafAI — Plant Health Monitoring
architecture.subtitle: How a leaf photo becomes a plant health result.
architecture.description: The image moves from the browser through the prediction API and model, then returns with a readable result. Select a component to see its role.

nodes.title: User
nodes.subtitle: Take or upload a photo
responsibilities: Take a leaf photo with the browser camera or choose one from a device.
Check the image before sending it for analysis.
Read the result and any warning that the prediction needs a closer look.

nodes.title: React / Vite
nodes.subtitle: Photo input and results
responsibilities: Shows the camera, upload, image preview and result screens.
Sends the selected image to the Flask API for prediction.
Displays the predicted condition, confidence, care advice and follow-up tools.

nodes.title: Flask REST API
nodes.subtitle: Connects the application
responsibilities: Accepts a leaf image through POST /predict.
Prepares the image, runs the model and builds the response.
Provides separate routes for plant guidance, reports, scan history and location information.
notes: The API returns a structured result so the interface can show the diagnosis, supporting information and review warnings together.

nodes.title: Preprocessing
nodes.subtitle: Prepare the image
responsibilities: Converts the uploaded image to RGB and resizes it to 128 × 128 pixels.
Applies the input processing expected by the MobileNetV2 model.
Adds a batch dimension so the model can process the image.
notes: The image must be prepared in the same way as the model's training inputs; a different scaling method can change its predictions.

nodes.title: MobileNetV2
nodes.subtitle: Classify the leaf
responsibilities: Loads the trained model when the API starts.
Scores the prepared image against 38 plant health classes across 14 species.
Passes class probabilities to the next step for interpretation.
notes: Training dataset: PlantVillage, sourced from Kaggle.
MobileNetV2 was adapted through transfer learning for this classification task.
Model training and evaluation happen separately from a visitor's scan. An upload uses the saved model for inference.

nodes.title: Prediction processing
nodes.subtitle: Explain the model output
responsibilities: Keeps the three highest scoring classes and translates them into readable plant and condition names.
Checks the leading score and its gap from the next result.
Adds severity and care information to the prediction.
notes: A result is marked for review if its leading score is below 70% or less than 15 percentage points ahead of the runner-up.
The result is still shown, with a warning to try a clearer photo or consider similar conditions.

nodes.title: Results interface
nodes.subtitle: Present the diagnosis
nodes.technology: Flask JSON response · React results UI
responsibilities: Shows the likely plant condition, confidence score and severity.
Includes alternative predictions and a warning when the result is uncertain.
Provides care guidance, a healthy leaf reference, follow-up chat and report export.

nodes.title: Knowledge base
nodes.subtitle: Plant care context
nodes.technology: Python knowledge dictionaries · Reference image files
responsibilities: Supplies condition descriptions, treatment and prevention guidance.
Adds plant information such as climate, soil and suitable regions.
Provides healthy reference images and material for follow-up questions.

nodes.title: Plant Doctor
nodes.subtitle: Ask about a result
responsibilities: Uses the current scan and the visitor's question as context.
Draws on plant care information to answer follow-up questions.
Can use an optional Groq service for explanations and falls back to local responses when it is unavailable.
notes: The external explanation service is optional; plant guidance remains available without it.

nodes.title: PDF reports
nodes.subtitle: Save a scan summary
responsibilities: Lets visitors export the result from the report preview.
Includes the condition, confidence, severity and guidance in the report.
Also provides a separate API route for generating a PDF.
notes: The report preview exports a PDF in the browser. The API's PDF route is a separate option.

nodes.title: Performance
nodes.subtitle: Metrics and scan history
responsibilities: Shows available model performance information and a confusion matrix.
Summarizes previous scans by confidence, severity and predicted condition.
Keeps monitoring views separate from the steps used to make one prediction.
notes: Performance figures belong to the model version they were measured on. They should not be read as accuracy for a different saved model.

nodes.title: File storage
nodes.subtitle: Scans and uploads
responsibilities: Saves prediction records in a JSON file and uploaded photos on the server's filesystem.
Keeps cached performance information and scan history in JSON files.
notes: The application uses local files for this data. The current Render configuration does not specify a persistent disk, so scan history may not survive a redeployment.

requestPath.title: Send it for analysis
requestPath.description: The browser sends the image to POST /predict.

decisions.title: Use MobileNetV2 for image classification
decisions.description: Transfer learning let the team adapt an existing image model to 38 plant health classes instead of training a new network from scratch. The saved model scores each photo submitted for analysis.

decisions.title: Prepare every image the same way
decisions.description: The API converts photos to RGB, resizes them to 128 × 128 pixels and applies MobileNetV2's expected input processing. Consistent input keeps the live prediction path aligned with the trained model.

decisions.title: Show uncertainty alongside a prediction
decisions.description: The interface keeps the top three possibilities. A leading score below 70%, or a gap under 15 percentage points to the next class, adds a review warning so visitors can judge how much confidence to place in the result.

decisions.title: Add care information after classification
decisions.description: The model identifies a likely condition; separate plant knowledge supplies treatment, prevention and environmental context. This keeps the prediction result useful without presenting the model as a source of care advice.

decisions.title: Use files for project data
decisions.description: Uploaded photos and scan records are stored as files, with prediction history in JSON. This keeps the project simple, but the current hosting setup does not guarantee that local files persist across deployments.

decisions.title: Keep model evaluation separate from scanning
decisions.description: Training and evaluation happen before the model is deployed. A visitor's scan runs inference only, and performance figures should be tied to the exact model version that produced them.

projects.title: AURAK's Dine Ordering System
projects.contribution: Contributed to full-stack development as part of a six-person team, including menu management interfaces and connecting the application to its backend and database.
projects.keyFeature: Cafeteria pre-ordering with Stripe checkout and role-based tools for staff to manage menu listings and product images.
projects.technicalChallenge: Connecting the React frontend, Express backend, and PostgreSQL database, then configuring the application to run on Render with a Neon-hosted database.
projects.summary: A cafeteria pre-ordering website built by a six-person team, with online payments through Stripe and menu management tools for staff.
projects.problem: Students need a convenient way to place cafeteria orders in advance, while staff need a simple way to keep menu listings and product images up to date.
projects.solution: Built a React frontend connected to a Node.js and Express backend with PostgreSQL. The application brings together pre-ordering, Stripe checkout, and role-based menu management, with deployment on Render and database hosting on Neon.
highlights: Stripe-based checkout was included in the team’s ordering workflow.
Built role-based CMS interfaces for menu listings and product images
Automated deployment with render.yaml and a serverless Neon PostgreSQL database

caseStudy.description: A web-based ordering system for AURAK's dine, allowing students to browse the menu, place orders and pay online, with a content management system for staff to manage menu items and product images.
features: Deployed on Render with Neon database

projects.title: Photography Portfolio
projects.summary: A curated collection of my photography, showcasing composition, light, motion, and color through visual storytelling.
projects.problem: I wanted to show the creative decisions behind my photographs, from intentional framing and exposure to the mood of the final edit.
projects.solution: Curated themed galleries with notes on the story, shooting process, and techniques behind each image.
projects.contribution: Photographed, edited, and selected the images, using leading lines, natural light, controlled motion, and color grading to shape each collection.
projects.keyFeature: Themed photo collections with image stories, process notes, and the photography skills demonstrated.
projects.technicalChallenge: Balancing highlights and shadows in mixed light, controlling motion blur, and keeping color and mood consistent across a collection.
stackBreakdown: Composition: leading lines, visual balance, and intentional framing
Camera control: exposure balance, panning, and motion blur
Editing: highlight recovery, contrast, and color grading
highlights: Photography across architecture, automotive, landscapes, and everyday scenes
Creative process and techniques documented alongside the images
Curated collections shaped by light, atmosphere, and visual storytelling
